formalized_ms: The reverse logarithmic Kodaira inequality and additivity
gap: Lean is only the negative-fiber branch of a companion paper's log additivity; no orbifold/log/ordinary Iitaka subadditivity at all.
quote: The finite-dimension and negative-base branches of the paper's additivity theorem are outside this selected statement.

gap: Lean: explicit degree-20 cone is not spectrahedral (no LMI). Headline: no semidefinite lift with auxiliary variables; that explicit cone does have one.
quote: The formalized counterexample is an explicit homogeneous polynomial of degree $20$ in $23$ real variables.

formalized_ms: Two limit cycles for quintic Liénard systems
gap: Lean covers only quintic classical Liénard systems (≤2 cycles, attained); the headline's uniform bound B(d) for all planar polynomial fields is absent.
quote: the formalized result proves that every real polynomial $F$ of degree at most five yields at most two limit cycles, and that some such $F$ yields exactly two.

formalized_ms: A logarithmic independence bound for clique-free graphs
gap: Lean lacks the O_F(Δ/logΔ) correspondence-coloring bound; the AEKS bound follows from it via max-degree deletion, so Lean is implied (weaker, not different).
quote: For every fixed integer $r\ge4$, there is $c_r>0$ such that every finite $K_r$-free simple graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $d\ge2$ has an independent set of size at least $c_r n\log d/d$.

formalized_ms: Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability
gap: Lean is only part (i), the colored-graph criterion; it lacks undecidability (ii), the nonrepresentable lattice (iii) and subgroup intervals (iv).
quote: This selected theorem is the equivalence with the graph criterion; the paper's undecidability and subgroup-interval conclusions are outside it.

formalized_ms: Buffered comparison and stopping-band resolution in critical Ising
gap: Lean is a finite-graph likelihood comparison lemma (an input to the universality papers); it has no scaling limits, CFT correlations or SLE3 convergence.
quote: The paper's finite stopping-band approximation theorem is outside this selected statement.

formalized_ms: Optimal-order mixing of the Thorp shuffle
gap: Only explicit constants missing: ThorpRemaining states t_mix=Θ(log N) and 2048d/32800d convergence, but not 1600d or the 2d−O(1) lower bound.
quote: After $1600d$ complete shuffles, the full permutation law converges in total variation to uniform as $d\to\infty$, uniformly over initial decks. Together with the support lower bound of $2d-O(1)$, this gives mixing time $\Theta(d)=\Theta(\log(2^d))$.

gap: Lean is the scalar (m=1) case only; it lacks matrix-valued potentials of every size and the classification of all equality cases.
quote: The formalized result determines the sharp one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring constant for $1/2<\gamma<3/2$.

formalized_ms: Threshold parallel repetition for finite-dimensional entangled games
gap: Lean rate exponent is δ^13, the paper's universal rate is δ^5; the note states δ^13 without saying it is weaker than the paper's.
quote: the probability of winning at least the fraction $v+\delta$ of $k$ repetitions is at most $\exp(-\kappa\delta^{13}k/(1+\log(|A||B|)))$ for one universal $\kappa>0$.

formalized_ms: A counterexample to the coarse Novikov conjecture
gap: Lean kills the class only under reduced assembly; the headline needs vanishing in maximal Roe algebra K-theory (stronger, since reduced factors through maximal).
quote: Its degree-one coarse $K$-homology contains an infinite-order class whose image under ordinary coarse assembly into the reduced locally compact Roe algebra vanishes.

formalized_ms: Weak Hessian bounds along every geodesic in RCD spaces
gap: Lean is the auxiliary weak-Hessian-along-geodesics theorem; it does not give the Alexandrov ⇔ RCD + distributional sectional curvature characterization.
quote: The formalization transfers a weak Hessian upper bound to every prescribed minimizing geodesic in an $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ space with finite $N>1$.
